effects-feel: shimmer passes come and go like sun through moving cloud (#324)

* effects-feel: shimmer passes come and go like sun through moving cloud (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Passes are events on half-period slots; slow sky noise decides whether a
slot holds one and how bright it is, so sunny spells bring passes close
together (sometimes overlapping, brighter wins) and cloudy ones leave the
row still for periods on end. Each pass crosses at its own pace.

* effects-feel: under cloud the shimmer thins to faint passes, never gone for long (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Review high on #324: dark spells reached 876 s at the default period; the
sky now has a presence floor and cloudy passes are faint, so the longest
spell over four hours is ~5 min. The lookback is derived from the timing
constants it depends on. Shimmer tests now check band width and interior
still spells; the readability window covers twelve periods.

docs(highlighter): a declined call name can take a later pattern's style (rich-highlighter-058y)
fix(highlighter): a < before a long name with no > takes one pass (rich-highlighter-058y)

fix(highlighter)!: highlighting takes one pass over a long run (rich-highlighter-058y)

Three of Rich's patterns rescan a run from each of its characters, so a
100k-cell run took 5s (letters, `<`) to 75s (digits) to highlight:

- `call` looked for a `(` from every letter of a word. It now starts only
  where a word does. A name glued to the end of another match mid-word
  (`foo` in `aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-fffoo(`) is no longer styled as a call; this
  is the one change in output, documented in docs/highlighting.md.
- the number patterns' `[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*` could split a digit run any way.
  `[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?` matches the same strings in the same order.
- `tag` can only open at the text's first `<`; a lookbehind starts it there.

A 600k-input differential fuzz against the old patterns found no
difference in JSONHighlighter and, in ReprHighlighter, only glued calls.
